summary: Job 1 (22 verses) continues the story of suffering. Starting with 'There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.', it moves through themes of suffering, justice and calls readers toward God's wisdom.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows suffering lived out in land of uz, poetic dialogue. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
Yahweh said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power. Only on himself don’t stretch out your hand.” So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh.
In all this, Job didn’t sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through suffering and justice, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 5 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'It was so, when the days of their feasting had run their course, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the n...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about suffering. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
